defs.def: a person who admires sb/sth or enjoys watching or listening to sb/sth very much 迷；狂热爱好者；狂热仰慕者

ex.s: Even soccer fans tend to have a seat each; gone are the days of thousands standing to watch the match.
ex.t: 就连足球迷也倾向于每人有一个座位；成千上万人站着观看比赛的日子一去不复返了。

ex.s: TOKNOW Magazine is a big hit in the world of children’s publishing, bringing a unique combination of challenging ideas and good fun to young fans every month.
ex.t: TOKNOW 杂志在儿童出版界大受欢迎，每月都为年轻的读者粉丝带来兼具挑战性思想与趣味的独特组合。

ex.s: SoFi Stadium is the go-to destination in the heart of Los Angeles for sports fans.
ex.t: SoFi体育场位于洛杉矶市中心，是体育迷们的首选目的地。

ex.s: Even the biggest sausage fan doesn’t want to eat them every day.
ex.t: 即便是最大的香肠爱好者，也不想每天都吃香肠。

ex.s: On 30 May, after the preparations were complete, the day finally came when the pandas met their fans for the first time.
ex.t: 5 月 30 日，所有准备工作就绪后，熊猫们终于迎来了与它们的粉丝首次见面的日子。

ex.s: Now I spend three weeks out of every month traveling and have over 464,000 fans following me online.
ex.t: 现在，我每个月有三周时间在旅途中度过，有超过 46.4 万的粉丝在线关注我。

ex.s: This is something that even the highly successful Harry Potter movies can’t escape from, with fans of the books disappointed not to see some of their favourite characters in the movie versions.
ex.t: 这甚至是极为成功的《哈利\u00b7波特》电影也无法逃脱的，书迷们因为在电影中没有看到一些他们最喜欢的角色而感到失望。

ex.s: You do not have to be a fan to recognise the skill of professional players - how they use their bodies to pass, score and defend can be amazing to see - or to fell the excitement of a game ending with a surprising twist.
ex.t: 你不必是球迷，也能看得出职业选手的技巧——他们如何用身体来传球、得分和防守，看起来令人惊叹——也能感受到以出人意料的转折结束的一场比赛所带来的兴奋。

ex.s: We could also say Even if you are not a football fan, it can be amazing to watch professional players use their bodies to pass, score and defend.
ex.t: 我们也可以说 即使你不是足球迷，看到职业球员用他们的身体来传球、得分和防守，也可能令人惊叹。

defs.def: a machine with blades that go round to create a current of air 风扇
a thing that you hold in your hand and wave to create a current of cool air 扇子
to make air blow onto sb/sth by waving a fan, your hand, etc. 扇（风）
to make a fire burn more strongly by blowing on it 扇，吹（使火更旺）
to make a feeling, an attitude, etc. stronger 煽起；激起
